source_title: PayPal's Seller Protection Program (United States) - Last updated on January 26, 2026
verification_note:
The official legal-hub page was downloaded and read in full on 2026-10-04 (HTML as served, SHA-256 e7123028b4ddc194183ed747fb4398a5e76c501d365f256bb37a843004f168e3; the page is dynamic, so the hash identifies that download only). It says 'Last updated on January 26, 2026'. The page text contains no signature requirement and no monetary threshold for signed proof of delivery; the proof-of-delivery list asks for a verifiable tracking number, date of delivery with 'delivered' status, and a recipient address matching the Transaction Details shipping address. That the signature requirement was REMOVED on 2026-01-26 is NOT stated on the page: it is inferred from the absence of the requirement, so the removal itself is unverified. The PayPal US User Agreement (useragreement-full, last updated on September 14, 2026) only points to this page for the program terms. Checks with basis published_policy cite the section headings of the page; checks the page does not state are app_quality_rule and are never shown as a PayPal requirement.
2026-10-06 (RULES-US1): eligibility_notes added, three rows whose quotes are the page's own sentences verbatim (sections 'What’s Eligible', 'Ineligible Items and Transactions', 'Basic Requirements'), read from the 2026-10-06 download (SHA-256 7cb604bec3a445cd2a920beb1a57f9e814b66134bd8a878719b03a3ea4cf574b, still 'Last updated on January 26, 2026'); they are informational and change no check.
2026-10-07 (FIX-RONDA4): whitespace only, no quote edited. The page's HTML (the 2026-10-06 download above, SHA-256 7cb604bec3a445cd2a920beb1a57f9e814b66134bd8a878719b03a3ea4cf574b) has two non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) in each of three eligibility_notes strings: the snad_not_eligible lead_in ('transactions' + U+00A0 + 'are', 'not' + U+00A0 + 'eligible'), the snad_not_eligible quote ('a' + U+00A0 + 'Significantly', 'Described' + U+00A0 + 'claim).') and the unauthorized_shipment_within_two_days quote ('of' + U+00A0 + 'Unauthorized', 'Transaction' + U+00A0 + 'claim,'); this file keeps ordinary spaces there on purpose, as the kept plain-text extract of the same download does (private evidence, sha256 195cfcfdd3dbf039783947903afd307618b09f8c64c138f9e1bb188837704c88). Comparisons of these strings with the page fold U+00A0 to a space. The other string, the inr_card_issuer_chargeback quote, is exact against the page HTML.
2026-10-19 (RC43-PK W1-3): a `clause` object added to the six published_policy checks (tracking_number, delivery_status, delivery_date, destination, full_address, signature). Each quote is copied verbatim from the 2026-10-06 page text extract, section 'Establishing Proof of Shipment or Proof of Delivery' (Physical Goods). The signature clause quotes the heading of the proof list, which names no signature, as the check's citation says. No citation, check or eligibility_notes row was edited.
signature_limits_note: The US page lists no signed-receipt threshold, so there is no per-currency table. signature_required=false makes the signature check not_applicable. If PayPal reintroduces a threshold, add signature_limits and set signature_required to true in a new dated rule set.
basic_requirements_not_checked_by_app: Primary address of the seller's PayPal account is in the United States (section 'Basic Requirements').
Item is a physical, tangible good (or meets the intangible-goods requirements).
Seller responds to PayPal's requests for documentation in the time requested.
Pre-ordered or made-to-order goods ship within the listed timeframe; otherwise shipping within 7 days of payment is recommended.
Item was not redirected to a different address after shipping (section 'Basic Requirements').

eligibility_notes.note: Claim-level exclusions and conditions the page states, shown to the seller as information when the dispute's own fields match the trigger. They are not checks: they never change a check's state and never say whether PayPal will grant protection. Matching is done by code on the dispute object PayPal returned (copilot/core/eligibility.py).
eligibility_notes.trigger_source: PayPal Customer Disputes API v1, OpenAPI document info.version 1.12, components.schemas.dispute.properties reason (schema dispute_reason) and dispute_channel (schema dispute_channel); schema.json pinned 2026-10-06, SHA-256 fee5e04ab606f8961b95744e65c4189fc7c4613e79ba2f944d2deab79e834330

rows.quote: Item Not Received claims that result from buyers filing chargeback claims with their issuers for card-funded transactions are not eligible for PayPal’s Seller Protection.

rows.lead_in: The following items or transactions are not eligible for PayPal’s Seller Protection program:
rows.quote: Items where the buyer claims (either with us or their card issuer) that the item you sent isn’t what was ordered (referred to as a Significantly Not as Described claim).

In the case of Unauthorized Transaction claim, you must provide valid proof of shipment or proof of delivery that demonstrates that the item was shipped or provided to the buyer no later than two days after PayPal notified you of the dispute or reversal.
